control_naming_note: Critical controls expose usable accessible names and role/state information that match the task the voter is actually taking.
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes remain understandable through landmarks, headings, usable control names, and announced state changes rather than assuming visual layout alone carries the answer.
error_and_status_announcement_note: Validation and correction states are exposed in a way assistive technologies can detect without forcing the voter to rediscover the page by guesswork.
heading_structure_note: Headings and section labels are descriptive enough that the current answer, warning, and help lanes remain understandable when traversed out of visual order.
landmark_structure_note: Critical answer/help regions are exposed through semantic sections or labeled landmarks so nonvisual users can identify the main route and fallback lanes quickly.
live_update_announcement_note: Lookup results, warnings, and route-state changes become nonvisually apparent through bounded status/live-region handling or other coherent announcement patterns.
manual_help_contact_note: A visible and announceable first-party help/contact lane remains available when the main route becomes ambiguous in nonvisual use.
relationship_and_instruction_note: Required-field cues, grouped options, helper text, and related instructions remain programmatically associated or explicitly textual rather than conveyed only by styling or proximity.
same_answer_across_modalities_note: Nonvisual semantics may change traversal and announcement cues but do not silently change the underlying authoritative answer.
